en: The *Sūtra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas of the Future Constellation Kalpa*, also titled *The Collection of the Great Mountains of Merit of All Buddhas*.
The translator’s name is lost; it is now appended to the Liang dynasty records.
Indeed, when one cultivates goodness, blessings arrive; when one commits evil, calamities follow. The principles are brilliantly clear, yet those who believe and awaken [to them] are rare.

Alas! Having already been born together in this world of the five turbidities, the afflictions of the five aggregates and the three poisons blaze fiercely, causing us to revolve through birth and death without end.

In the past, when the Buddha was in the world, the number of people was like the sands of the Ganges; now they have gradually declined and diminished, so that not one in ten thousand remains. Why is this so?

It is because those who do good are few, while those who commit evil are many; upon death they fall into the three miserable realms, becoming entirely fish, insects, or animals, no longer obtaining human bodies.
Therefore, the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* states:
"The three evil realms will be filled, while the hosts of devas and humans will diminish.
Before long, the kalpa will come to an end; this long-term decline is truly lamentable."

Therefore, the Tathāgata teaches and transforms according to the various regions, emphasizing compassion and valuing goodness; by not sparing even one's own life, practicing with diligent vigor, and performing the labor of prostrating and bowing the head to the crown of the Buddha, one may attain deliverance. Such devotion can eliminate the sins of immeasurable kalpas; as sin is extinguished and merit arises, one reaches the state of non-action (*asaṃskṛta*).

In this future Constellation Eon (*Nakṣatra-kalpa*), there shall appear one thousand Buddhas whose names are as follows. If anyone hears these names and worships them with single-minded devotion, without fear of error, they will surely attain *nirvāṇa*, forever leave behind the sufferings of birth and death within the three miserable realms, abide securely in loving-kindness and patience, and become fully endowed with great learning.

If there are those who can receive, uphold, study, and recite this, such persons will certainly encounter a thousand Buddhas in succession; they shall attain the extinction of the heavy sins of birth and death accumulated over immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, and shall obtain the supernatural powers, samādhis, and unimpeded eloquence of all Buddhas.

Regarding all the great Dharma-gates, the gates of dhāraṇī, and the various wisdoms of all scriptures, you should preach the Dharma according to what is appropriate without ever giving rise to deception;
remain free from fame and profit, harbor no jealousy, practice the six points of harmonious respect, uphold them with a single mind, and do not lose these conditions.
A practitioner who acts in this manner will swiftly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. [The preceding prose section is absent from the original manuscript.

The Tathāgata Śaila.
From this point upward, there are one thousand future Buddhas.

If there are sons or daughters of noble family who, upon hearing the names of these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, rejoice with faith and delight, uphold, recite, and read them without slandering them; or if they are able to transcribe them and explain them to others; or if they are able to fashion their images and establish them; or if they are able to make offerings of incense, flowers, and music, extol the merits of the Buddhas, and pay homage with a sincere heart—this is superior to taking the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, filling them with precious jewels and pure maṇi pearls piled as high as the Brahma-heaven, and bestowing them as gifts for hundreds of thousands of kalpas.

These sons and daughters of noble family have already made offerings to this Tathāgata in the past; having subsequently attained these merits through rebirths, they shall continue until they become Buddhas without end, and all shall receive the prediction of enlightenment from the Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa.

Wherever such a person is born, they will always encounter the Triple Gem and attain birth in the buddha-fields of all Buddhas. Their six sense faculties will be complete, and they will not fall into the eight difficult conditions. They will swiftly come to be fully endowed with the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics. If one can even once prostrate oneself on the ground with the five limbs touching and pay homage, declaring aloud:
"I now universally pay homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time; I now universally pay homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time."
After reciting this a thousand times, one should then rise; the merit and blessings obtained will be as described above.
Taking this merit, one should vow that all sentient beings of the five realms who are subject to impermanence may be born in the Land of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life.
One should establish this great vow so that all sentient beings may be born in that realm.

Having been born in that land, their physical marks and signs of excellence, as well as their wisdom and eloquence, will be like those of Amitābha Buddha, the Honored One of all worlds; the karmic fruits they obtain will also be equal to those of the World-Honored One.
